title: Tensors hold numbers
summary: A tensor is a number container with a shape. It can be a single number, a list or a table.
introduction: A tensor is a number container with a shape. It can be a single number, a list or a table. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A tensor is a number container with a shape. It can be a single number, a list or a table.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Examples need Python and TensorFlow in a separate local environment. Some installations are large; follow the official supported-platform guide. No paid API or cloud account is needed.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of TensorFlow. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
import tensorflow as tf

x = tf.constant([2, 4, 6])
print(x.numpy().tolist())
blocks.title: Tensors hold numbers

blocks.text: The output is [2, 4, 6]. numpy exposes the eager tensor values; tolist makes the result easy to read.
